text: 和平，奋斗，救中国
pinyin: hé píng, fèn dòu, jiù zhōng guó
literal: peace, struggle, save · China
natural: Peace, struggle, save China

meaning.en: The words reported as Sun Yat-sen's last testament in 1925, urging peace and perseverance for the sake of the nation.
meaning.zh: 据记载为孙中山1925年临终时的遗言，勉励后人以和平与奋斗拯救中国。

equivalents: peace, struggle, save China
a dying statesman's final charge

examples.zh: 纪念馆的墙上写着孙中山的临终遗言“和平，奋斗，救中国”。
examples.en: On the wall of the memorial hall are Sun Yat-sen's dying words, 'Peace, struggle, save China'.

examples.zh: 历史课上，老师带全班朗读了和平，奋斗，救中国这句遗言。
examples.en: In history class the teacher had everyone read aloud the last words 'Peace, struggle, save China'.

story.en: Sun Yat-sen (1866-1925) died in Beijing on 12 March 1925; 'Peace, struggle, save China' are the words recorded by those with him as his last.
story.zh: 孙中山（1866—1925）1925年3月12日在北京逝世，“和平，奋斗，救中国”是身边人记录的临终之语。

usage.en: Quoted in commemorations of Sun Yat-sen and in speeches about national renewal. The words are reported by those at his bedside in March 1925; accounts of the exact wording vary slightly.
usage.zh: 纪念孙中山和谈论民族复兴时常被引用。这几个字是1925年3月他病榻旁的人所记录的遗言，具体措辞各书略有出入。

text: 著述最谨严，非徒中国小说史；遗言太沉痛，莫作空头文学家
pinyin: zhù shù zuì jǐn yán, fēi tú zhōng guó xiǎo shuō shǐ, yí yán tài chén tòng, mò zuò kōng tóu wén xué jiā
literal: writings · most · rigorous, not · merely · Chinese · fiction · history; last words · too · grievous, don't · be · empty-headed · literary man
natural: his writing was most rigorous, not just a history of Chinese fiction; his last words were so grave: do not be an empty man of letters

meaning.en: Cai Yuanpei's elegiac couplet for Lu Xun: it praises his rigorous scholarship and recalls his dying warning against empty literary posturing.
meaning.zh: 蔡元培挽鲁迅联：称赞鲁迅著述严谨，不只是一部《中国小说史略》，又痛惜其遗言，告诫人勿作空头文学家。

equivalents: a tribute to a rigorous writer
no empty literati

examples.zh: 蔡元培的挽联“著述最谨严，非徒中国小说史；遗言太沉痛，莫作空头文学家”，评价极高。
examples.en: Cai Yuanpei's couplet, 'rigorous in writing, more than a history of fiction; solemn in last words, be no empty man of letters', is high praise.

examples.zh: 展厅里挂着蔡元培的挽联：著述最谨严，非徒中国小说史；遗言太沉痛，莫作空头文学家。
examples.en: In the exhibition hall hangs Cai Yuanpei's elegiac couplet: 'rigorous in writing, more than a history of fiction; solemn in last words, be no empty man of letters'.

story.en: Lu Xun died in Shanghai on 19 October 1936; the educator Cai Yuanpei (1868-1940) sent this couplet as an elegy.
story.zh: 1936年10月19日鲁迅在上海逝世，教育家蔡元培（1868—1940）撰此联致挽。

usage.en: A quoted funeral couplet from 1936, literary and formal. 非徒 = 'not merely'; 《中国小说史》 refers to Lu Xun's 《中国小说史略》. Quoted in writing about Lu Xun or about literary integrity; the second line is the more often quoted.
usage.zh: 1936年的挽联，书面、庄重。“非徒”即“不但”；“中国小说史”指鲁迅的《中国小说史略》。谈论鲁迅或文人操守时引用，下联更常被引。

text: 我从山中来，带着兰花草
pinyin: wǒ cóng shān zhōng lái, dài zhe lán huā cǎo
literal: I · from · mountain · in · come, bring · orchid · grass
natural: I came from the mountains, bringing an orchid plant

meaning.en: The opening of Hu Shi's poem 'Hope' (also known as 'Orchid'), a gentle vernacular verse about planting a wild orchid and waiting for it to bloom.
meaning.zh: 胡适《希望》的开头，写带着山中的兰花草回家种在小园里，盼它早日开花。

equivalents: I came from the hills bringing an orchid
a wild orchid brought home

examples.zh: 这首歌的第一句是“我从山中来，带着兰花草”。
examples.en: The first line of the song is 'I came from the mountains, bringing an orchid plant'.

examples.zh: 音乐课上，同学们唱起了我从山中来，带着兰花草。
examples.en: In music class the students sang 'I came from the mountains, bringing an orchid plant'.

story.en: The poem 'Hope' (《希望》), whose 'Orchid' (《兰花草》) title is that of the later song, is by Hu Shi (1891-1962), a pioneer of vernacular Chinese poetry.
story.zh: 《希望》（后以《兰花草》之名谱成歌曲）是白话新诗倡导者胡适（1891—1962）的作品。

usage.en: A well-known early vernacular poem, famous today mainly as the song 《兰花草》 set to music in Taiwan. Quoted as a gentle, nostalgic opening line.
usage.zh: 白话新诗的名篇，今天多因谱曲后的歌曲《兰花草》而广为人知。常作温柔、怀旧的开头引用。

text: 红杏枝头春意闹，著一闹字而境界全出
pinyin: hóng xìng zhī tóu chūn yì nào, zhuó yī nào zì ér jìng jiè quán chū
literal: red · apricot · branch · tip · spring · feeling · bustles, put · one · bustle · word · and · world · wholly · emerges
natural: on the apricot's red branch spring bustles; with the one word 'bustle' the whole scene comes alive

meaning.en: Wang Guowei's praise of Song Qi's line: the single word 闹 ('bustle') is enough to bring the whole spring scene to life.
meaning.zh: 王国维评宋祁词句：只用一个“闹”字，整个春景的意境就全都出来了。

equivalents: one word brings the whole scene to life
le mot juste

examples.zh: 王国维说“红杏枝头春意闹，著一闹字而境界全出”，赞的是炼字之妙。
examples.en: Wang Guowei's remark that 'the one word 闹 brings the whole scene out' praises the art of choosing the exact word.

examples.zh: 语文老师以红杏枝头春意闹，著一闹字而境界全出为例，讲解炼字。
examples.en: The Chinese teacher used 'the one word 闹 brings the whole scene out' as an example of choosing words.

story.en: In 《人间词话》 (Remarks on Poetry, 1908-09) Wang Guowei (1877-1927) comments on Song Qi's line 红杏枝头春意闹 from the lyric 《玉楼春》.
story.zh: 王国维（1877—1927）在《人间词话》（1908—1909）中评点宋祁《玉楼春》中的“红杏枝头春意闹”一句。

usage.en: A standard quotation in writing on word choice (炼字) and poetic atmosphere (境界). The quoted poem line is from Song Qi's 《玉楼春》. 著 here is read zhuó ('to put in').
usage.zh: 谈炼字和意境时的常用引文。所引词句出自宋祁《玉楼春》。“著”在此读 zhuó，意为“用上”。

text: 凡一代有一代之文学
pinyin: fán yí dài yǒu yí dài zhī wén xué
literal: every · one · age · has · one · age · 's · literature
natural: every age has a literature of its own

meaning.en: Wang Guowei's view of literary history: each dynasty has its own characteristic literary form, such as Tang poetry, Song lyrics and Yuan drama.
meaning.zh: 王国维的文学史观：每个时代都有自己代表性的文学，如唐诗、宋词、元曲。

equivalents: each age has its own literature
every era its own literary form

examples.zh: 王国维说“凡一代有一代之文学”，后来成了讲文学史的常用语。
examples.en: Wang Guowei's 'every age has a literature of its own' became a stock phrase in literary history.

examples.zh: 唐诗、宋词、元曲，正应了凡一代有一代之文学这句话。
examples.en: Tang poetry, Song lyrics and Yuan drama bear out the saying 'every age has a literature of its own'.

story.en: Wang Guowei's study of Song and Yuan drama (1912) opens its preface with this line, followed by 'the Chu elegies, Han rhapsodies, Tang poetry, Song lyrics and Yuan songs'.
story.zh: 王国维1912年的宋元戏曲研究，序言开篇即此句，下接“楚之骚，汉之赋……唐之诗，宋之词，元之曲”。

usage.en: Used in lessons and writing on Chinese literary history, often as a prelude to 唐诗、宋词、元曲. In the original the line continues with a list of forms (楚之骚，汉之赋…). The book is now usually titled 《宋元戏曲史》; 《宋元戏曲考》 is its earlier title.
usage.zh: 常用于讲授和书写中国文学史，多引出“唐诗、宋词、元曲”。原文接着列举各代文体（楚之骚，汉之赋……）。该书今多称《宋元戏曲史》，《宋元戏曲考》是早期书名。

text: 手空空，无一物；路遥遥，无止境
pinyin: shǒu kōng kōng, wú yī wù, lù yáo yáo, wú zhǐ jìng
literal: hands · empty · empty, without · one · thing; road · far · far, without · end
natural: empty-handed, owning nothing; the road ahead long, with no end

meaning.en: Lines from the song of New Asia College in Hong Kong, written by Qian Mu: the founders began with nothing, facing an endless road.
meaning.zh: 钱穆为香港新亚书院所作校歌中的句子：创办之初一无所有，前路漫长无尽。

equivalents: empty-handed, with a long road ahead
nothing in hand, no end to the road

examples.zh: 新亚书院的院歌里有一句“手空空，无一物；路遥遥，无止境”。
examples.en: The New Asia College song has the line 'empty-handed, owning nothing; the road long, without end'.

examples.zh: 创业之初他常念起手空空，无一物；路遥遥，无止境这两句歌词。
examples.en: At the start of his venture he often recalled the lyrics 'empty-handed, owning nothing; the road long, without end'.

origin.source: 钱穆作词《新亚书院校歌》

story.en: Qian Mu (1895-1990), who founded New Asia College in Hong Kong in 1949 with very scant resources, wrote the words of its college song.
story.zh: 钱穆（1895—1990）1949年在香港以极简陋的条件创办新亚书院，并为校歌作词。

usage.en: Quoted to express starting from nothing and facing a long road, often at college events or by Hong Kong and overseas Chinese communities. The chunk's unpunctuated form 手空空无一物，路遥遥无止境 is also seen. Qian Mu (1895-1990) founded New Asia College in 1949.
usage.zh: 用来表达白手起家、前路漫漫，常见于书院活动及港台海外华人社群。无标点的“手空空无一物，路遥遥无止境”也常见。钱穆（1895—1990）1949年创办新亚书院。

text: 当信任何一国之国民，对其本国以往历史，应该略有所知
pinyin: dāng xìn rèn hé yì guó zhī guó mín, duì qí běn guó yǐ wǎng lì shǐ, yīng gāi lüè yǒu suǒ zhī
literal: should · believe · any · one · country · 's · citizens, toward · their · own · country · past · history, ought · slightly · have · what · know
natural: one should hold that the citizens of any country ought to know something of their own country's past

meaning.en: Qian Mu's first article of faith for readers of his national history: citizens of any country should have at least some knowledge of its past.
meaning.zh: 钱穆对读《国史大纲》者提出的第一条信念：任何一国的国民，都应对本国以往的历史略有所知。

equivalents: every citizen should know something of the nation's history
know your own country's past

examples.zh: 钱穆在《国史大纲》引论中写道：当信任何一国之国民，对其本国以往历史，应该略有所知。
examples.en: In the introduction to his 'Outline of National History' Qian Mu wrote that citizens of any country should have some knowledge of their own history.

examples.zh: 谈到历史教育，他引用了“当信任何一国之国民，对其本国以往历史，应该略有所知”。
examples.en: On history education, he quoted: 'citizens of any country should know something of their own country's past'.

story.en: Qian Mu's 《国史大纲》 (Outline of National History, 1940) opens its introduction with a list of beliefs readers should hold; this is the first.
story.zh: 钱穆《国史大纲》（1940）的引论开头列出读者应先具备的几条信念，此为第一条。

usage.en: A quoted sentence, frequently cited in discussions of history education and national identity. 当信 here means 'one should hold the belief that', not 'should trust'.
usage.zh: 常在谈论历史教育和国民认同时引用。这里的“当信”意为“应当相信”，不是“应当信任”。

text: 愿中国青年都摆脱冷气，只是向上走
pinyin: yuàn zhōng guó qīng nián dōu bǎi tuō lěng qì, zhǐ shì xiàng shàng zǒu
literal: wish · Chinese · youth · all · shake off · cold air, just · keep · upward · walk
natural: may China's young people all shake off the chill and simply keep moving upward

meaning.en: Lu Xun's appeal to young people to ignore cynicism and defeatism and just keep striving upward.
meaning.zh: 鲁迅对青年的寄语：不要理会冷嘲热讽和自暴自弃的论调，只管向上走。

equivalents: shake off the cynics and strive upward
keep moving upward

examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，校长引用了鲁迅的话：愿中国青年都摆脱冷气，只是向上走。
examples.en: At the graduation ceremony the principal quoted Lu Xun: 'May China's young people shake off the chill and simply keep moving upward.'

examples.zh: 面对网上的冷嘲热讽，他想起了“愿中国青年都摆脱冷气，只是向上走”。
examples.en: Facing cynicism online, he recalled 'may China's young people shake off the chill and simply keep moving upward'.

origin.source: 鲁迅《热风·随感录四十一》

story.en: From 'Random Thoughts No. 41' in the essay collection 《热风》 (Hot Wind), written by Lu Xun (1881-1936) in 1919 and followed by 'give one part of light for every part of warmth'.
story.zh: 出自鲁迅（1881—1936）1919年所作杂文集《热风》中的《随感录四十一》，下文为“有一分热，发一分光”。

usage.en: Often quoted to young people. The next lines are equally famous: 有一分热，发一分光 ('give as much light as you have warmth'). 冷气 means cold, cynical talk.
usage.zh: 常用来勉励青年。紧接着的“有一分热，发一分光”同样有名。“冷气”指冷嘲热讽、消极丧气的话。

text: 我向来是不惮以最坏的恶意，来推测中国人的
pinyin: wǒ xiàng lái shì bù dàn yǐ zuì huài de è yì, lái tuī cè zhōng guó rén de
literal: I · always · am · not · fear · with · worst · 's · ill will, to · speculate · Chinese people · [particle]
natural: I have never hesitated to judge my countrymen with the worst of ill will

meaning.en: Lu Xun's bitter statement after the 1926 shooting of student protesters: he has always been ready to assume the worst of people, yet even he had not expected this cruelty.
meaning.zh: 鲁迅在1926年学生请愿遭枪杀后写下的沉痛之语：他向来不怕以最坏的恶意推测国人，却没想到竟残忍到这个地步。

equivalents: I have never shrunk from thinking the worst
assuming the worst of people

examples.zh: 鲁迅写道“我向来是不惮以最坏的恶意，来推测中国人的”，其后是更深的悲愤。
examples.en: Lu Xun wrote 'I have never hesitated to judge my countrymen with the worst ill will', followed by deeper grief and anger.

examples.zh: 课文里有一句：我向来是不惮以最坏的恶意，来推测中国人的，同学们讨论了很久。
examples.en: The text has the line 'I have never hesitated to judge my countrymen with the worst ill will', and the class discussed it for a long time.

origin.source: 鲁迅《华盖集续编·记念刘和珍君》

story.en: In this 1926 essay Lu Xun mourns Liu Hezhen and other students killed on 18 March 1926 in Beijing, and writes that he had never imagined such cruelty.
story.zh: 鲁迅1926年撰文悼念在3月18日北京请愿中遇害的刘和珍等学生，文中写到自己没有料到竟会如此残忍。

usage.en: Quoted in discussions of Lu Xun's critique of national character and of the Liu Hezhen incident (18 March 1926). Note 推测, not 揣测; the sentence goes on 然而我还不料，也不信竟会下劣凶残到这地步. 惮 is read dàn.
usage.zh: 谈论鲁迅的国民性批判和“三一八”惨案时引用。注意是“推测”而非“揣测”；下文为“然而我还不料，也不信竟会下劣凶残到这地步”。“惮”读 dàn。

text: 无穷的远方，无数的人们，都和我有关
pinyin: wú qióng de yuǎn fāng, wú shù de rén men, dōu hé wǒ yǒu guān
literal: endless · 's · distant place, countless · 's · people, all · with · me · have · connection
natural: the endless distance and countless people all have something to do with me

meaning.en: Lu Xun's late statement of social concern: however far away, every place and every person is connected to him.
meaning.zh: 鲁迅晚年的名句，表达他的社会关怀：无论多远的地方、多少陌生的人，都与自己息息相关。

equivalents: no one is a stranger to me
everything in the world concerns me

examples.zh: 这位记者常说，无穷的远方，无数的人们，都和我有关。
examples.en: The reporter often says, 'the endless distance and countless people all have to do with me'.

examples.zh: 毕业赠言里，老师抄下了“无穷的远方，无数的人们，都和我有关”。
examples.en: In the graduation message the teacher copied out 'the endless distance and countless people all have to do with me'.

origin.source: 鲁迅《且介亭杂文末编·“这也是生活”……》

story.en: Lu Xun (1881-1936) wrote the essay 'This Too Is Life...' in 1936, during his last illness, and it is collected in 《且介亭杂文末编》.
story.zh: 鲁迅（1881—1936）1936年病中写下《“这也是生活”……》，收入《且介亭杂文末编》。

usage.en: Quoted to express social responsibility and a wide sympathy, often by journalists, volunteers and teachers. It comes from Lu Xun's last year of writing (1936).
usage.zh: 用来表达社会责任感和广阔的同情心，记者、志愿者、教师常引用。出自鲁迅生命最后一年（1936）的文章。

text: 深蓝的天空中挂着一轮金黄的圆月，下面是海边的沙地，都种着一望无际的碧绿的西瓜
pinyin: shēn lán de tiān kōng zhōng guà zhe yì lún jīn huáng de yuán yuè, xià miàn shì hǎi biān de shā dì, dōu zhòng zhe yí wàng wú jì de bì lǜ de xī guā
literal: deep · blue · 's · sky · in · hangs · one · wheel · golden · 's · round · moon, below · is · seaside · 's · sand land, all · planted · boundless · 's · emerald · 's · watermelon
natural: in the deep blue sky hangs a golden full moon, and below, on the seaside sand, boundless emerald watermelons

meaning.en: A famous passage from Lu Xun's story 'My Old Home': the narrator's boyhood memory of a moonlit watermelon field by the sea.
meaning.zh: 鲁迅小说《故乡》中的名段：“我”回忆少年时海边沙地月夜瓜田的美景。

equivalents: a moonlit watermelon field
a boyhood scene of the countryside

examples.zh: 《故乡》里“深蓝的天空中挂着一轮金黄的圆月，下面是海边的沙地，都种着一望无际的碧绿的西瓜”，是几代学生背过的段落。
examples.en: 'My Old Home' contains the passage 'in the deep blue sky hangs a golden full moon, and below, on the seaside sand, boundless emerald watermelons', which generations of students have memorised.

examples.zh: 她描写家乡的夏夜时，想起了“深蓝的天空中挂着一轮金黄的圆月，下面是海边的沙地，都种着一望无际的碧绿的西瓜”。
examples.en: Describing a summer night at home, she was reminded of 'in the deep blue sky hangs a golden full moon, and below, on the seaside sand, boundless emerald watermelons'.

story.en: The short story 《故乡》 (My Old Home, 1921) by Lu Xun (1881-1936) recalls the narrator's friendship with the peasant boy Runtu.
story.zh: 鲁迅（1881—1936）的短篇小说《故乡》（1921）回忆“我”与农家少年闰土的友谊。

usage.en: A famous textbook descriptive passage, studied in school and imitated in composition lessons. It is the boyhood image of Runtu in the story, set against the grim present. In the text it continues with a boy holding a steel pitchfork.
usage.zh: 著名的课文描写段落，学生在学校学习并仿写。这是小说中少年闰土的形象，与凄凉的现实形成对照。原文接着写一个手捏钢叉的少年。

text: 不必说碧绿的菜畦，光滑的石井栏，高大的皂荚树，紫红的桑椹
pinyin: bù bì shuō bì lǜ de cài qí, guāng huá de shí jǐng lán, gāo dà de zào jiá shù, zǐ hóng de sāng shèn
literal: no · need · to say · emerald · 's · vegetable bed, smooth · 's · stone · well · rail, tall · 's · soap-pod · tree, purple-red · 's · mulberry
natural: not to mention the emerald vegetable beds, the smooth stone well-rail, the tall honey-locust tree, the purple-red mulberries

meaning.en: A famous passage from Lu Xun's memoir essay, listing the delights of the garden of his childhood home.
meaning.zh: 鲁迅回忆散文中的名段，列举儿时百草园里的种种乐趣。

equivalents: not to mention the lush garden
a child's paradise

examples.zh: 同学们都能背出“不必说碧绿的菜畦，光滑的石井栏，高大的皂荚树，紫红的桑椹”。
examples.en: The students can all recite 'not to mention the emerald vegetable beds, the smooth stone well-rail, the tall honey-locust tree, the purple-red mulberries'.

examples.zh: 他回忆外婆的菜园时，不禁想到不必说碧绿的菜畦，光滑的石井栏，高大的皂荚树，紫红的桑椹。
examples.en: Recalling his grandmother's vegetable patch, he thought of 'not to mention the emerald vegetable beds, the smooth stone well-rail, the tall honey-locust tree, the purple-red mulberries'.

origin.source: 鲁迅《从百草园到三味书屋》

story.en: The essay is in 《朝花夕拾》 (Dawn Blossoms Plucked at Dusk) by Lu Xun (1881-1936), written in 1926; it sets the joyful Hundred Plants Garden against the strict private school.
story.zh: 此文收入鲁迅（1881—1936）的《朝花夕拾》，作于1926年，将自由快乐的百草园与严格的私塾三味书屋对照。

usage.en: A famous textbook descriptive passage on childhood joy, much used as a model for listing sensory images. 不必说 introduces the delights taken for granted before turning to the less obvious ones.
usage.zh: 著名的课文描写段落，是排列感官意象的范例。“不必说”先带出人人皆知的乐趣，再转向更细微的趣味。

text: 在我的后园，可以看见墙外有两株树，一株是枣树，还有一株也是枣树
pinyin: zài wǒ de hòu yuán, kě yǐ kàn jiàn qiáng wài yǒu liǎng zhū shù, yī zhū shì zǎo shù, hái yǒu yī zhū yě shì zǎo shù
literal: at · my · back garden, can · see · wall · outside · have · two · trees, one · is · jujube tree, also · have · one · also · is · jujube tree
natural: in my back garden you can see two trees beyond the wall: one is a jujube tree, and the other is also a jujube tree

meaning.en: The famously plain opening of Lu Xun's prose poem 'An Autumn Night', whose deliberate repetition has been much discussed by readers.
meaning.zh: 鲁迅散文诗《秋夜》的著名开头，平淡中带着刻意的重复，常被读者议论。

equivalents: two trees, both jujubes
the famous repetition of Lu Xun

examples.zh: 《秋夜》的开头“在我的后园，可以看见墙外有两株树，一株是枣树，还有一株也是枣树”，常被拿来讨论修辞。
examples.en: The opening of 'An Autumn Night', 'in my back garden you can see two trees beyond the wall, one a jujube and the other also a jujube', is often discussed for its rhetoric.

examples.zh: 网上常有人模仿：在我的后园，可以看见墙外有两株树，一株是枣树，还有一株也是枣树。
examples.en: People online often imitate it: 'in my back garden you can see two trees beyond the wall, one a jujube and the other also a jujube'.

story.en: 'An Autumn Night' (1924) opens the prose-poem collection 《野草》 (Wild Grass) by Lu Xun (1881-1936).

usage.en: A famous textbook opening, often parodied or imitated for humour (e.g. 'one is X, and the other is also X'). Readers differ on its meaning, from loneliness to stubborn resilience.
usage.zh: 著名的课文开头，常被仿写或戏仿（如“一个是X，还有一个也是X”）。读者对其含义解读不一，有人读出孤寂，有人读出倔强。

text: 血债必须用同物偿还，拖欠得愈久，就要付更大的利息
pinyin: xuè zhài bì xū yòng tóng wù cháng huán, tuō qiàn de yù jiǔ, jiù yào fù gèng dà de lì xī
literal: blood · debt · must · with · same · thing · repay, owe · [particle] · more · long, then · must · pay · greater · 's · interest
natural: a blood debt must be repaid in kind, and the longer it is left unpaid, the more interest it will carry

meaning.en: Lu Xun's angry demand after the 18 March 1926 killings: blood debts can only be repaid in kind, and delay only adds interest.
meaning.zh: 鲁迅在1926年“三一八”惨案后的愤激之语：血的债只能用血偿还，拖得越久，代价越大。

equivalents: a debt of blood must be repaid in blood
the longer the debt is delayed, the higher the interest

examples.zh: 鲁迅写道“血债必须用同物偿还，拖欠得愈久，就要付更大的利息”。
examples.en: Lu Xun wrote that 'a blood debt must be repaid in kind, and the longer it is left unpaid, the more interest it will carry'.

examples.zh: 讲到历史的清算，他引了血债必须用同物偿还，拖欠得愈久，就要付更大的利息。
examples.en: On settling accounts with history, he quoted 'a blood debt must be repaid in kind, and the longer it is left unpaid, the more interest it will carry'.

origin.source: 鲁迅《华盖集续编·无花的蔷薇之二》

story.en: Written on 25 March 1926, a week after the 18 March shootings of unarmed petitioners in Beijing, by Lu Xun (1881-1936).
story.zh: 鲁迅（1881—1936）写于1926年3月25日，距北京“三一八”枪杀手无寸铁的请愿群众仅一周。

usage.en: Quoted in discussions of historical injustice and accountability, in a historical-reference tone. In the original there is a full stop after 偿还, with an exclamation at the end. Related to, but distinct from, the common saying 血债血偿.
usage.zh: 谈论历史上的冤案和责任追究时引用，多作历史引文。原文“偿还”后为句号，句末为感叹号。与常见的“血债血偿”相关，但是不同的词条。

text: 希望是本无所谓有，无所谓无的
pinyin: xī wàng shì běn wú suǒ wèi yǒu, wú suǒ wèi wú de
literal: hope · is · originally · not · so-called · exist, not · so-called · not exist · [particle]
natural: hope is originally neither said to exist nor said not to exist

meaning.en: Lu Xun's reflection at the end of 'My Old Home': hope is neither real nor unreal in itself, like a road that comes into being only when people walk it.
meaning.zh: 鲁迅《故乡》结尾的感悟：希望本来无所谓有，无所谓无，就像地上的路，是走的人多了才有的。

equivalents: hope is neither there nor not there
hope is what we make of it

examples.zh: 读到“希望是本无所谓有，无所谓无的”，他沉思了很久。
examples.en: Reading 'hope is originally neither said to exist nor not to exist', he fell into deep thought.

examples.zh: 在最困难的时候，她常想起希望是本无所谓有，无所谓无的这句话。
examples.en: In her hardest times she often thought of the line 'hope is originally neither said to exist nor not to exist'.

story.en: The closing passage of 《故乡》 (My Old Home, 1921) by Lu Xun (1881-1936), where the narrator reflects on hope as he leaves his hometown.
story.zh: 鲁迅（1881—1936）《故乡》（1921）的结尾段，“我”离开故乡时对希望的思考。

usage.en: Usually quoted together with the next line about the road: 其实地上本没有路，走的人多了，也便成了路. Commonly cited in essays about hope and perseverance.
usage.zh: 通常与下文“其实地上本没有路，走的人多了，也便成了路”一起引用。常见于谈论希望和坚持的文章。

text: 改良改良，越改越凉
pinyin: gǎi liáng gǎi liáng, yuè gǎi yuè liáng
literal: reform reform, the · more · reform · the · more · cold
natural: reform, reform, the more we reform the colder it gets

meaning.en: A quip from Lao She's play 'Teahouse': the more the shopkeeper tries to 'improve' things, the worse his fortunes get; 凉 (cold) hints at business going cold.
meaning.zh: 老舍话剧《茶馆》中的台词：越“改良”，生意越冷清，世道越不济。

equivalents: the more you reform, the worse it gets
improvements that only make things worse

examples.zh: 老板苦笑着说：改良改良，越改越凉。
examples.en: The boss said with a wry smile, 'reform, reform, the more we reform the colder it gets'.

examples.zh: 店里换了三次菜单，生意反倒冷清，真是改良改良，越改越凉。
examples.en: The shop changed its menu three times and business only dropped: truly, reform, reform, the more we reform the colder it gets.

story.en: Lao She's three-act play 《茶馆》 (Teahouse, 1957) follows the owner Wang Lifa, who keeps 'improving' his teahouse through decades of upheaval.
story.zh: 老舍的三幕话剧《茶馆》（1957）写掌柜王利发在几十年的动荡中不断“改良”自己的茶馆。

usage.en: A rhyming (良/凉 liáng) jibe used jokingly when changes make things worse. It is a line spoken by a character in Lao She's 《茶馆》, not Lao She's own statement; the exact staging and wording vary a little between editions.
usage.zh: 押韵（良、凉）的调侃，用于越改越糟的情形，多带幽默。这是《茶馆》中人物的台词，并非老舍本人的话；各版本措辞和场次略有出入。

text: 戴着脚镣跳舞
pinyin: dài zhe jiǎo liào tiào wǔ
literal: wear · [aspect] · shackles · dance
natural: dancing in shackles

meaning.en: Wen Yiduo's image for poetry written within strict formal rules: restrictions are what let a true artist show real skill.
meaning.zh: 闻一多用来比喻诗要受格律的约束：正是有了限制，才见出作者的功力。

equivalents: dancing in chains
creativity within constraints

examples.zh: 闻一多说作诗如同戴着脚镣跳舞，限制越多越见功力。
examples.en: Wen Yiduo said writing poetry is like dancing in shackles: the more the constraints, the more the skill shows.

examples.zh: 写命题作文，就像戴着脚镣跳舞。
examples.en: Writing an essay on an assigned topic is like dancing in shackles.

story.en: The essay 《诗的格律》 (1926) by the poet and scholar Wen Yiduo (1899-1946) argues for metre and form in new vernacular poetry.
story.zh: 诗人学者闻一多（1899—1946）1926年的论文《诗的格律》，主张白话新诗也应讲究格律。

usage.en: Today used more widely for working well under tight rules or limits, sometimes with a wry tone. Wen Yiduo used it in his essay on poetic form; the image is often said to echo a Western saying about verse and rules.
usage.zh: 今天泛指在严格规则或限制下仍做得出色，有时带自嘲。闻一多在论诗歌格律的文章里用此比喻，据说其意象与西方论诗的说法相呼应。

text: 微风过处，送来缕缕清香，仿佛远处高楼上渺茫的歌声似的
pinyin: wēi fēng guò chù, sòng lái lǚ lǚ qīng xiāng, fǎng fú yuǎn chù gāo lóu shàng miǎo máng de gē shēng shì de
literal: breeze · passes · where, sends · over · wisp · wisp · clear · fragrance, as if · distant · place · tall · building · on · faint · 's · song · like
natural: where the breeze passes it brings wisps of fragrance, like faint singing from a tall house far away

meaning.en: A famous simile from Zhu Ziqing's 'Moonlight over the Lotus Pond': the scent of lotus on the breeze is compared to distant, faint singing.
meaning.zh: 朱自清《荷塘月色》中的名喻：微风送来荷花的清香，像远处高楼上隐约的歌声。

equivalents: fragrance like distant song
a scent on the breeze

examples.zh: 《荷塘月色》里“微风过处，送来缕缕清香，仿佛远处高楼上渺茫的歌声似的”，是通感的经典例子。
examples.en: 'Moonlight over the Lotus Pond' contains 'where the breeze passes it brings wisps of fragrance, like faint singing from a tall house', a classic case of synaesthesia.

examples.zh: 语文课上讲通感，老师举了微风过处，送来缕缕清香，仿佛远处高楼上渺茫的歌声似的。
examples.en: Teaching synaesthesia, the teacher cited 'where the breeze passes it brings wisps of fragrance, like faint singing from a tall house'.

story.en: The essay 《荷塘月色》 (1927) by Zhu Ziqing (1898-1948) describes a night walk by the lotus pond on the Tsinghua campus.
story.zh: 朱自清（1898—1948）的散文《荷塘月色》（1927）写月夜在清华园荷塘边散步所见。

usage.en: A famous textbook descriptive passage, the standard example of 通感 (synaesthesia): smell described as sound. 缕缕 is read lǚ lǚ.
usage.zh: 著名的课文描写段落，是“通感”（以听觉写嗅觉）的经典例子。“缕缕”读 lǚ lǚ。

text: 东海西海，心理攸同；南学北学，道术未裂
pinyin: dōng hǎi xī hǎi, xīn lǐ yōu tóng, nán xué běi xué, dào shù wèi liè
literal: east · sea · west · sea, mind · reason · thereby · same; south · learning · north · learning, the Way · arts · not yet · split
natural: east sea and west sea share the same human mind; southern and northern learning have not been torn apart

meaning.en: Qian Zhongshu's opening claim in 'Tan yi lu': human minds are alike across East and West, and learning in every region shares one root.
meaning.zh: 钱钟书《谈艺录》序中的名句：东西方人的心理相通，南北各派的学术根本未曾分裂。

equivalents: East and West share one human mind
learning is one across cultures

examples.zh: 钱钟书以“东海西海，心理攸同；南学北学，道术未裂”开篇，申明中西互证的方法。
examples.en: Qian Zhongshu opened with 'East sea and west sea share one human mind; southern and northern learning are not split', declaring his method of comparing China and the West.

examples.zh: 比较文学课上，教授引用了东海西海，心理攸同；南学北学，道术未裂。
examples.en: In the comparative literature class the professor quoted 'east sea and west sea share one human mind; southern and northern learning are not split'.

story.en: The preface to 《谈艺录》 (Tan yi lu, 'On the Art of Poetry', 1948), the critical work by Qian Zhongshu (1910-1998), opens with this couplet.
story.zh: 钱钟书（1910—1998）的诗学著作《谈艺录》（1948）序言开篇即此联。

usage.en: A classical-style parallel couplet, often cited to justify comparative and cross-cultural study. 攸 = 所 ('that by which'); 道术 = the Way and its arts, i.e. learning as a whole. 《庄子·天下》 speaks of 道术将为天下裂, which this line answers.
usage.zh: 仿古的对偶句，常用来说明比较研究和跨文化研究的合理性。“攸”即“所”；“道术”指学术整体。《庄子·天下》有“道术将为天下裂”之语，此句与之相应。

text: 旁人若问其中意，且到寒斋吃苦茶
pinyin: páng rén ruò wèn qí zhōng yì, qiě dào hán zhāi chī kǔ chá
literal: bystander · if · ask · its · inner · meaning, just · come to · humble · studio · drink · bitter · tea
natural: if people ask what lies behind it, just come to my humble study and drink bitter tea

meaning.en: The closing couplet of Zhou Zuoren's 'Poem on My Fiftieth Birthday': asked about his meaning, he offers only a cup of bitter tea.
meaning.zh: 周作人《五十自寿诗》的结尾联：旁人若问诗中含意，他只请来书斋喝一杯苦茶。

equivalents: come and drink bitter tea and see
I'll say no more than this

examples.zh: 周作人在《五十自寿诗》里写道“旁人若问其中意，且到寒斋吃苦茶”。
examples.en: In his 'Poem on My Fiftieth Birthday' Zhou Zuoren wrote 'if people ask what lies behind it, just come to my humble study and drink bitter tea'.

examples.zh: 他不愿多解释，只笑着说：旁人若问其中意，且到寒斋吃苦茶。
examples.en: He did not want to explain; he just smiled and said, 'if people ask what lies behind it, come to my humble study and drink bitter tea'.

story.en: Zhou Zuoren (1885-1967) wrote this poem in 1934 for his fiftieth birthday; its tone drew both praise and criticism at the time.
story.zh: 周作人（1885—1967）1934年为五十寿辰作此诗，其情调在当时既受称赞也遭批评。

usage.en: Quoted when someone declines to explain, or in discussions of Zhou Zuoren's reclusive style and the debate over this 1934 poem. 寒斋 is a humble term for one's own study.
usage.zh: 用于不愿多作解释时，或谈论周作人的隐逸风格及围绕这首1934年诗作的争论。“寒斋”是对自己书斋的谦称。

text: 为什么我的眼里常含泪水？因为我对这土地爱得深沉
pinyin: wèi shén me wǒ de yǎn lǐ cháng hán lèi shuǐ, yīn wèi wǒ duì zhè tǔ dì ài de shēn chén
literal: why · my · eyes · in · often · hold · tears? because · I · toward · this · land · love · [particle] · deep
natural: why are my eyes so often filled with tears? Because my love for this land runs deep

meaning.en: The closing lines of Ai Qing's poem 'I Love This Land' (1938): his tears come from a deep love for his war-torn homeland.
meaning.zh: 艾青《我爱这土地》（1938）的结尾：他眼里常含泪水，是因为对饱经战乱的土地爱得深沉。

equivalents: tears of deep love for the homeland
my love for this land runs deep

examples.zh: 朗诵会上，他深情地念出“为什么我的眼里常含泪水？因为我对这土地爱得深沉”。
examples.en: At the poetry reading he recited with feeling, 'why are my eyes so often filled with tears? Because my love for this land runs deep'.

examples.zh: 离开家乡多年，他常想起为什么我的眼里常含泪水？因为我对这土地爱得深沉。
examples.en: Years after leaving home he often thought of 'why are my eyes so often filled with tears? Because my love for this land runs deep'.

story.en: Ai Qing (1910-1996) wrote 'I Love This Land' in Wuhan in November 1938, as the Japanese invasion deepened.
story.zh: 艾青（1910—1996）1938年11月在日军侵略日深之际于武汉写下《我爱这土地》。

usage.en: The most quoted lines of modern Chinese patriotic poetry, used in speeches, essays and recitals. Ai Qing wrote the poem in November 1938 during the war of resistance against Japan.
usage.zh: 中国现代爱国诗歌中被引用最多的诗句，常见于演讲、文章和朗诵会。艾青1938年11月抗日战争期间写下此诗。
